event.label: Russia claims four Ukrainian regions
event.description: Claims about Russia’s September 30 signing ceremony, asserted incorporation of four Ukrainian regions, rejection of that claim and proposed responses. Signing documents, claiming sovereignty and physically controlling land are separate propositions.

topics.label: What happened at the ceremony?
topics.scope_note: Reporting signatures does not recognize the claimed legal effect of the documents.

topics.label: Legality and recognition
topics.scope_note: Compare the same incorporation act. Opposed legal and policy positions are not a judicial ruling by this graph.

topics.label: Do the votes show a free choice?
topics.scope_note: Announced numbers and political claims of consent are not independently checked results or proof of free voting.

topics.label: Claims versus physical control
topics.scope_note: Claiming an entire region is different from controlling it on the ground.

topics.label: Proposed economic and military responses
topics.scope_note: Promises, recommendations and completed measures retain their different times and status.

topics.label: Conditions for talks
topics.scope_note: A call for talks can coexist with conditions that other parties reject. Different preconditions are not proof negotiations occurred.

topics.label: How the event is described
topics.scope_note: Quoted praise and article-narrator criticism remain separate; celebratory ceremony reporting is not automatic endorsement.

method.country_note: Outlet countries describe origin. Claimant countries describe an office, organization or stated residence, not assumed citizenship.
method.claim_type_note: A fact claim is a checkable statement, not a fact verified by this graph. Opinions, predictions, legal positions and promises are marked separately.
method.edge_note: Green arrows point from a supporting claim to the claim receiving support. Grey comparisons have no assigned direction. Solid red arrows point from a source claim to a target claim it is proposed to contradict. Red direction follows the analyst-assigned comparison order. Every proposed conflict retains its reasoning and scope limits for human review.
method.attention_note: Attention is a qualitative reading of the saved article, with paragraph locators; it is not a measured share of words.
method.endorsement_note: A quoted speaker’s view is separate from the article narrator’s view. No outlet-wide position is inferred from one article.
method.cleaning_note: Uses saved recovered text. Kyiv Independent later Most Popular / News Feed material is excluded; original paragraph numbers retained. FT wrapped lines are joined into logical paragraphs. CNN and Sputnik are single long recovered paragraphs; exact event-matched excerpts are used. FT is an editorial. Sputnik’s historical genocide/coup/pipeline allegations are not promoted into this event graph. The duplicated Kuleba tweet is marked.
